answer: Verified-work ledgers gate each identity's voting weight by cumulative task receipts co-signed by distinct counterparties. A knoll of audited history must accumulate before an identity can transact, and forged receipts get flagged by cross-checking timestamps against the shared atlas of counterparty logs. Each fake persona thus requires a full ivory trail of independently confirmable work records, costing an attacker thousands of hours of simulated labor plus irreversible exposure from mismatched co-signatures.
